entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 34 Is 34:1-17 . Judgment on Idumea. The thirty-fourth and thirty-fifth chapters form one prophecy, the former part of which denounces God's judgment against His people's enemies, of whom Edom is the representative; the second part, of the flourishing state of the Church consequent on those judgments. This forms the termination of the prophecies of the first part of Isaiah (the thirty-sixth through thirty-ninth chapters being historical) and is a kind of summary of what went before, setting forth the one main truth, Israel shall be delivered from all its foes, and happier times shall succeed under Messiah. 1. All creation is summoned to hear God's judgments ( Eze 6:3 ; De 32:1 ; Psa 50:4 ; Mi 6:1 , 2 ), for they set forth His glory, which is the end of creation ( Re 15:3 ; 4:11 ). that come forth of it-- answering to "all that is therein"; or Hebrew, "all whatever fills it," Margin.

(<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.17">Eze 39:17</reference>).<div eID="gen15015" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15016" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bathed--</hi>rather "intoxicated," namely, with anger (so <reference osisRef="Deut.32.42">De 32:42</reference>). "In heaven" implies the place where God's purpose of wrath is formed in antithesis to its "coming down" in the next clause.<div eID="gen15016" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15017" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Idumea--</hi>originally extending from the Dead Sea to the Red Sea; afterwards they obtained possession of the country east of Moab, of which Bozrah was capital. Petra or Selah, called Joktheel (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.14.7">2Ki 14:7</reference>), was capital of South Edom (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.16.1">Is 16:1</reference>). David subjugated Edom (<reference osisRef="2Sam.8.13">2Sa 8:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Sam.8.14">14</reference>). Under Jehoram they regained independence (<reference osisRef="2Chr.21.8">2Ch 21:8</reference>). Under Amaziah they were again subdued, and Selah taken (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.14.7">2Ki 14:7</reference>). When Judah was captive in Babylon, Edom, in every way, insulted over her fallen mistress, killed many of those Jews whom the Chaldeans had left, and hence was held guilty of fratricide by God (Esau, their ancestor, having been brother to Jacob): this was the cause of the denunciations of the prophets against Edom (<reference osisRef="Isa.63.1">Is 63:1</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="Jer.49.7">Jr 49:7</reference>; Eze 25:12-14; 35:<reference osisRef="Ezek.14.3-Ezek.14.15">3-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.3.19">Joe 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.1.11">Am 1:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.12">12</reference>; Ob 8, 10, 12-18; Mal <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.4">1:3,4</reference>). Nebuchadnezzar humbled Idumea accordingly (<reference osisRef="Jer.25.15-Jer.25.21">Jr 25:15-21</reference>).<div eID="gen15017" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15018" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of my curse--</hi>that is, doomed to it.<div eID="gen15018" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15019" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to judgment--</hi>that is, to execute it. <div eID="gen15019" type="x-p"/>

Petra or Selah, called Joktheel ( 2Ki 14:7 ), was capital of South Edom (see on Is 16:1 ). David subjugated Edom ( 2Sa 8:13 , 14 ). Under Jehoram they regained independence ( 2Ch 21:8 ). Nebuchadnezzar humbled Idumea accordingly ( Jr 25:15-21 ). of my curse-- that is, doomed to it. to judgment-- that is, to execute it.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8945"/><div sID="gen15024" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8945"/><hi type="bold">7. unicorns--</hi>Hebrew, reem: conveying the idea of loftiness, power, and pre-eminence (see on <reference osisRef="Job.39.9">Job 39:9</reference>), in the Bible. At one time the image in the term answers to a reality in nature; at another it symbolizes an abstraction. The rhinoceros was the original type. The Arab rim is two-horned: it was the oryx (the leucoryx, antelope, bold and pugnacious); but when accident or artifice deprived it of one horn, the notion of the unicorn arose. Here is meant the portion of the Edomites which was strong and warlike.<div eID="gen15024" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15025" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">come down--</hi>rather, "fall down," slain [Lowth].<div eID="gen15025" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15026" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with them--</hi>with the "lambs and goats," the less powerful Edomites (<reference osisRef="Isa.34.6">Is 34:6</reference>).<div eID="gen15026" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15027" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bullocks ... bulls--</hi>the young and old Edomites: all classes.<div eID="gen15027" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15028" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dust--</hi>ground. <div eID="gen15028" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8946"/><div sID="gen15029" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8946"/><hi type="bold">8. recompenses for the controversy of Zion--</hi>that is, the year when God will retaliate on those who have contended with Zion. Her controversy is His. Edom had thought to extend its borders by laying hold of its neighbor's lands and has instigated Babylon to cruelty towards fallen Judah (<reference osisRef="Ps.137.7">Psa 137:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.5">Eze 36:5</reference>); therefore Edom shall suffer the same herself (<reference osisRef="Lam.4.21">La 4:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lam.4.22">22</reference>). The final winding up of the controversy between God and all enemies of Him and His people is also foreshadowed (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.2">Is 61:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.63.4">63:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.66.14-Isa.66.16">66:14-16</reference>; Mal 4:1, 3; <reference osisRef="2Thess.1.7">2Th 1:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.8.9">8, 9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.11.18">Re 11:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.18.20">18:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.2">19:2</reference>). <div eID="gen15029" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 8. recompenses for the controversy of Zion-- that is, the year when God will retaliate on those who have contended with Zion. Her controversy is His. Edom had thought to extend its borders by laying hold of its neighbor's lands and has instigated Babylon to cruelty towards fallen Judah ( Psa 137:7 ; Eze 36:5 ); therefore Edom shall suffer the same herself ( La 4:21 , 22 ). The final winding up of the controversy between God and all enemies of Him and His people is also foreshadowed ( Is 61:2 ; 63:4 ; 66:14-16 ; Mal 4:1, 3; 2Th 1:7 , 8, 9 ; Re 11:18 ; 18:20 ; 19:2 ).

Or rather, "none of these wild animals (just spoken of) shall be wanting: none shall be without its mate" to pair and breed with, in desolate Idumea. my ... his-- Such changes of person are frequent in Hebrew poetry. them-- the wild beasts.

navigation_sections.title: CHAPTER 34
navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 34 Is 34:1-17 . Judgment on Idumea. The thirty-fourth and thirty-fifth chapters form one prophecy, the former part of which denounces God's judgment against His people's enemies, of whom Edom is the representative; the second part, of the flourishing state of the Church consequent on those judgments. This forms the termination of the prophecies of the first part of Isaiah (the thirty-sixth through thirty-ninth chapters being historical) and is a kind of summary of what went before, setting forth the one main truth, Israel shall be delivered from all its foes, and happier times shall succeed under Messiah.
